title: Non-soficity of OpenAI's torsion-free hyperbolic group
description:
Is every word-hyperbolic group sofic? This was an open question. OpenAI recently constructed a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G that is not residually finite, and formalized that theorem in Lean. We show that G is not sofic. Their rank argument against finite quotients uses a finite quotient only through its permutation matrices, and it survives approximation: a relation that holds on all but a small fraction of points costs a small rank error, and a word with few fixed points costs a small trace error. The argument therefore excludes approximate permutation models at a fixed positive accuracy, while soficity would provide such models at every accuracy. Moreover, one fixed nonidentity element of G dies under every homomorphism from G to a sofic group, and G is neither LEF nor residually amenable.

The same rectangles and the same finite-field certificate also exclude Linnell division rings. Let q be the prime fixed by the construction. For every division ring K of characteristic q, the group ring K[G] has no Linnell division ring, and neither has the group ring over K of any group containing G. Freeness of certain line subgroups of G would force full rank, and the certificate forces the rank to collapse; no zero divisor is exhibited. OpenAI's torsion-free group with zero divisors over F_2 already shows that Linnell division rings need not exist in characteristic two; here the group is G itself. We also show that G is the free product of a free group and a finitely presented torsion-free hyperbolic group to which the same applies, that G is not bi-orderable, and that G embeds in no fundamental group of a two-complex with nonpositive immersions, and we make precise what the argument says about hyperlinearity.

The group and every input to the non-soficity argument are OpenAI's. Our contribution is the approximate rank argument, with explicit constants, its counterpart for division rings, and a Lean formalization of the non-soficity statement on top of OpenAI's development: some torsion-free word-hyperbolic group is not sofic.
